name: NutriRoute Street Cart Vendor Layered Stand
description: The uniform of a street food vendor working the Circuit grid — someone running a licensed cart or stall in one of M88's transit interchange markets, feeding the shift-change crowds with hot food and fast service. The foundation is a waterproof apron in deep charcoal with two wide kangaroo pockets at the hip, adjustable neck strap, and a NutriRoute vendor association logo embroidered in orange thread at the chest — a small circular badge marking the cart as part of the licensed vendor collective, not a black-market operation. Beneath the apron is a long-sleeve work shirt in navy with rolled-up cuffs, moisture-wicking, with a slim right-arm channel for basic neural port access (a concession to the vendor scanning their own BCI orders without removing layers). A thick-strapped canvas chest-cross — two straps meeting at a central ring — holds a compact insulated carry bag on the back for moving between the cart and supply drops. Trousers are charcoal utility cut, non-slip-treated at the knee, with a phone-sized side pocket sealed with a flap button. Footwear is a chunky slip-resistant clog-boot in black rubber composite, oil- and grease-proof, with a thick insole for standing twelve-hour shifts on concrete. A hairnet or close-cropped beanie in white covers the head — vendor association health code requirement. Hands are bare or in thin grip-texture food-service gloves, usually tucked into the apron pocket between uses.
functionality: Non-slip boot sole for wet cart surfaces, moisture-wicking shirt for high-heat cooking environments, insulated back carry bag for supply runs, BCI neural port access channel in shirt sleeve, wide apron pockets for order tools and payment devices, slip-proof trouser knee treatment for crouching at low cart storage.
what_it_says: Licensed, legitimate, and working every hour the transit system runs. The NutriRoute badge means they passed the vendor collective's health inspection and paid their monthly association fee — they have something to protect. The worn clog-boot soles mean they've been standing on this particular corner long enough to know every regular's order before they open their mouth.
manufacturer: NutriRoute Vendor Collective (apron and badge issued by collective; shirt and trousers from Hollenbeck workwear line; boots generic composite)
price_range: Φ140–Φ200 (apron collective-issued at membership; remainder self-purchased)
story_hooks: A vendor's NutriRoute badge is a near-perfect counterfeit — but they've been working the same corner for two years, and everyone on the block knows them. Someone gave them that badge, and that someone is now calling in a favor.

The insulated back carry bag has a false bottom. The vendor has been moving something other than food supplies between the cart and the supply depot for six months, and they're terrified of being caught.

A transit interchange vendor witnessed something at the platform level during a night shift and has been wearing their apron hood pulled low ever since — they're trying to look like a different person, and it's almost working.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, utilitarian silhouette built for endurance and function. The layered vendor uniform reads as grounded and no-nonsense — a charcoal apron over navy sleeves creates visual mass at the torso, anchored by sturdy boots. The chest-cross harness adds industrial geometry. Overall impression: hardworking, licensed, reliable.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the body for movement and airflow during long shifts; the apron hangs straight without tapering. Trousers are straight-cut utility, not slim. Sleeves are full-length but rollable. The chest harness sits snug but not restrictive. Everything designed for 12-hour standing shifts.
physical_description.primary_material: Waterproof synthetic-blend apron (DWR-treated canvas), moisture-wicking cotton-poly work shirt, treated utility cotton trousers with non-slip grip zones, oil-resistant rubber composite boots, reinforced canvas chest harness
physical_description.texture: Apron fabric is smooth and water-resistant with a subtle weave; work shirt has a soft matte finish with subtle ribbing; trousers have a matte utility texture with reinforced knee panels; boots are textured rubber with a grippy sole pattern
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep charcoal apron and trousers form the foundation; navy work shirt underneath; black rubber boots; white beanie/hairnet; bright orange embroidered NutriRoute logo at chest; natural tan/cream canvas harness with metal ring fittings
physical_description.closures: Apron: adjustable neck strap with slide-lock, side ties (or magnetic snap). Shirt: standard buttons, right sleeve has discrete friction-fit port access panel. Trousers: side zip or button fly, sealed flap pocket with single button. Boots: slip-on with elastic gusset. Chest harness: friction-fit ring closure.
distinctive_features: NutriRoute vendor collective logo embroidered in orange at chest — official licensing mark
Waterproof deep-charcoal apron with two oversized kangaroo pockets for cash, orders, tools
Slim neural-port access channel on right arm (BCI-friendly design)
Canvas chest-cross harness for insulated carry bag during supply runs
Non-slip knee treatment on utility trousers — faded from repeated wear
Thick-soled oil-proof clog-boot rated for 12+ hour standing shifts
Mandatory white hairnet or close-cropped beanie (vendor health code compliance)
Thin food-service gloves tucked into apron pocket (never worn unless actively handling food)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 (working class, licensed vendor collective member) — not black-market, not corpo, but established enough to wear official branding
physical_description.cultural_context: Street food vendor in the GLMZ transit interchange markets. Signals legitimate, registered operator, part of the NutriRoute collective. Wearing this means you're feeding shift-change crowds, you know the supply chains, you're networked into M88's arterial commerce. Not a corpo, not struggling — employed and visible.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in but maintained. Apron has grease spots that won't wash out and a slight permanent bend from the shape of the kangaroo pockets. Sleeves rolled and re-rolled every shift, so creases at the elbows. Trousers knees are faded from leaning and kneeling. Boots are scuffed and stained but regularly cleaned — the rubber stays resilient. The whole outfit smells faintly of food and industrial cleaner.

image_prompt: A tired-eyed figure in deep charcoal work apron and navy rolled-sleeve shirt stands in a neon-lit M88 transit market stall, forearms resting on a worn counter. Close-up of the torso shows the orange-embroidered NutriRoute vendor logo at chest, waterproof apron with visible grease marks, and a tan canvas chest harness with metal ring. Thick black clog-boots planted firmly on concrete, one foot slightly forward in a standing-all-day stance. Harsh overhead fluorescent strips cast shadows under the eyes; the beanie is white, practical, regulation. In the soft-focus background, holographic menu boards flicker and other vendor stalls glow. Shallow depth of field on the apron's kangaroo pockets and the wear pattern at the knees. Moody, industrial, authentic working-class GLMZ aesthetics. --ar 2:3 --v 6
